summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, and G-tube dependence was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and inability to maintain oral intake, leading to dehydration and acute kidney injury. She was hydrated with IV fluids, which resolved her renal dysfunction. Persistent nausea and decreased G-tube output prompted imaging, which revealed malposition of the tube tip in the duodenum. The tube was successfully replaced with a shorter one positioned in the stomach antrum, improving venting. During admission, she reported suicidal ideation, which was evaluated by psychiatry; it was determined to be partially attention-seeking, and a sitter was discontinued after she expressed future-oriented goals. Nutrition support was limited by lack of insurance coverage for TPN and ethanol lock line care. She was discharged home with improved pain, stable mental status, and instructions to eat small meals, maintain hydration, and follow up with her outpatient team.
problems: Dyspepsia and other specified disorders of function of stomach
